newsitem.title: USA: Asarco moves to trim concentrate inventories.
newsitem.headline: Asarco moves to trim concentrate inventories.

text.p: Asarco Inc said Monday it will partially curtail operations at one of the two concentrators at its Ray Complex to reduce copper concentrate inventories.

"The curtailment will begin October 8 and is expected to last through March 1997," chief executive Richard de J. Osborne said. "This curtailment will permit the company to process excess concentrates through its smelters.
"Mine production of copper in concentrates has exceeded the company's smelting capacity in recent months," he said.
Under normal circumstances the company buys or sells this intermediate form of copper in the world market to balance its inventory position, it pointed out.

Currently, however, there is a shortage of world smelter capacity and the resulting high treatment and refining charges make the sale of concentrates uneconomic, Asarco explained. The temporary curtailment will allow the company to process the concentrates internally and bring inventories back to normal levels, it said.
Despite the curtailment, the company said, Asarco expects its 1996 copper mine production to exceed 1 billion pounds.

The curtailment will reduce expected annual copper mine production by approximately 1-1/2 percent in both 1996 and 1997, Asarco said. There will be no effect on the company's smelter or refined copper production.

About 80 employees at the Ray Complex will be affected by this curtailment. Roughly one-third of these employees will be reassigned to other openings at the Ray Complex, Asarco said. The employees affected may also be considered for temporary positions should they become available at other Asarco operations. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
